standard.name: DesConOps
standard.subtitle: Design, construct and operate as one production system, and what ten verified changes a day would take

releases.name: Release 1: issue for construction
releases.description: Model, requirements and product keys cross together, before anything is fabricated or poured.

releases.name: Release 2: handover
releases.description: The asset record crosses as data, before the operator inherits the building.

steps.name: Requirement
steps.crosses: Owner need stated as checkable rules.

steps.name: Model
steps.crosses: Geometry and attributes keyed to place.

steps.name: Coordinate
steps.crosses: Issues exchanged and closed between tools.

steps.name: Issue for construction
steps.crosses: Model, requirements and product keys cross together.

steps.name: Plan
steps.crosses: Work packages keyed to place and product.

steps.name: Build
steps.crosses: Installed work recorded against the package.

steps.name: Capture
steps.crosses: Change, RFI and decision bound to place.

steps.name: Handover
steps.crosses: Asset record crosses as data, not binders.

steps.name: Run and monitor
steps.crosses: Telemetry keyed to the same places.

steps.name: Learn
steps.crosses: Operating data fed back to the next requirement.

contract.input: Each step takes a keyed input.
contract.check: It is checked against a published requirement.
contract.gate: It passes a gate held by someone with authority.
contract.record: It emits a record with its provenance.

designRules.rule: The gate goes before the irreversible step, not after it.
Standardize the interface, not the tool. Each firm keeps its own software.
Feedback crosses projects, not sprints, and the learning unit is the portfolio.

metrics.name: Verified handoffs a day
metrics.definition: Changes that crossed an interface and passed the gate with evidence, per project per day.

metrics.name: Design change to verified install
metrics.definition: Calendar days from a decision recorded in design to the installed, inspected result.

metrics.name: Rework per verified install
metrics.definition: Share of verified installs later reworked, by cause.

metrics.name: RFI cycle time
metrics.definition: Days from question to answer with authority.

crosswalk.asks: Owner requirements as IDS, with product class and cost on the same key.
Test on every issue, not at milestones.

gaps.name: A shared release gate
gaps.description: A release gate that carries model, requirement and product key together across the firms it joins.

gaps.name: The specification-to-product crosswalk
gaps.description: A published join from a specification section to the product classes that satisfy it.

gaps.name: The operate-to-design loop
gaps.description: Operating data keyed to the same places and fed back to the next requirement as checkable rules.

roles.name: Owners
roles.today: Bear most of the loss and receive the record last.
roles.withSharedRecord: Requirements written once as checkable rules at the start of design. Every model, submittal and handover is tested against them, and the owner holds one record across every release, so nothing is re-keyed at handover.
roles.proof: Requirements met at handover without manual re-entry, and change orders traced back to the requirement they changed.

roles.name: General contractors
roles.today: Live at the handoff where everything upstream lands at once.
roles.withSharedRecord: RFIs answered from the record before they are written, and design changes delivered to the field as verified changes, with the decision and its authority attached.
roles.proof: RFI cycle time in hours, not days, and fewer RFIs per million dollars of work.

roles.name: Architects
roles.today: Write the specification that every product decision depends on.
roles.withSharedRecord: Each specification section linked to the open product classes that satisfy it, so a submitted product is checked against the specification automatically.
roles.proof: First-pass submittal approval rates, and fewer substitution RFIs.

roles.name: Engineers
roles.today: Carry the coordination load inside the model.
roles.withSharedRecord: Every model issue checked against the information requirements, and every coordination issue closed against the shared record rather than inside one tool.
roles.proof: Clashes and missing information caught at issue, not discovered on site.

roles.name: Specialty contractors and fabricators
roles.today: Turn the design into physical parts, and are the first to pay when the data is wrong.
roles.withSharedRecord: Product data that arrives already classified, and shop drawings, model and product class kept in one record from order to installation.
roles.proof: Fewer wrong-product orders, and less re-fabrication from late changes.

roles.name: Operators
roles.today: Inherit the building and, today, a binder.
roles.withSharedRecord: The asset record delivered as live data at handover, and operating data fed back to the next design.
roles.proof: Time to a usable asset record after handover, and how often design decisions on the next project cite operating data from the last.

translation.equivalent: Information requirements checked on every model issue.
Issues exchanged between tools, then approval with authority.
RFIs, rework and lessons fed back to design.
